question: Refer to the exhibit. Which two statements about the routing table of the leaf switch are true? (Choose two.)
context:
ACI-Leaf1# show ip route vrf DATACENTER:DC
10.20.1.0/24, ubest/mbest: 1/0, attached, direct, pervasive
  *via 10.0.8.65%overlay-1, [1/0], 4w3d, static
172.16.100.0/24, ubest/mbest: 1/0
  *via 10.1.168.95%overlay-1, [200/5], 3w0d, bgp-132, internal, tag 132 (mpls-vpn)
172.16.99.0/24, ubest/mbest: 1/0
  *via 10.0.1.14, [20/0], 3w0d, bgp-132, external, tag 200
options: 10.20.1.0/24 is a BD subnet in ACI.
The next hop 10.0.1.14 for route 172.16.99.0/24 is the TEP address of a border leaf in ACI.
172.16.100.0/24 is a BD subnet in ACI.
The next hop 10.1.168.95 for route 172.16.100.0/24 is the TEP address of a border leaf in ACI.
The next hop 10.0.8.65 for route 10.20.1.0/24 is the TEP address of a border leaf in ACI.
theory: In an ACI fabric, a route marked "attached, direct, pervasive" is a bridge domain subnet hosted locally on that leaf via the pervasive (anycast) gateway SVI, so 10.20.1.0/24 is a BD subnet. External prefixes learned through an L3Out are redistributed into MP-BGP and installed with a next hop over the infra VXLAN overlay (overlay-1); that next-hop address is the TEP (tunnel endpoint) address of the border leaf that owns the external route, which is why 10.1.168.95 (tagged bgp-132/internal/mpls-vpn) is a border-leaf TEP for 172.16.100.0/24. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 4 — ACI Fabric and Bridge Domains)
